Exercise: Full Range-Of-Motion Lat Pulldown

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
pull

Difficulty Level:
intermediate

Movement Patterns:

- vertical_pulling

Primary Muscles:

- lats

Secondary Muscles:

- biceps
- middle back
- shoulders

Equipment:

- cable

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate to high

Recovery Time:
48 hours

Goals:
None

Contraindications:

- condition: Shoulder impingement, reason: May exacerbate symptoms
- condition: Lower back pain, reason: Slight arch in lower back may aggravate condition

Exercise Variations:

- name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown, primaryMuscles: ['lats', 'middle back']
- name: Narrow-Grip Lat Pulldown, primaryMuscles: ['lats', 'biceps']

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Barbell Pull-Down, equipment: barbell
- exercise_name: Machine Lat Pulldown, equipment: lat pulldown machine

Instructions:

- Either standing or seated on a high bench, grasp two stirrup cables that are attached to the high pulleys. Grab with the opposing hand so your arms are crisscrossed about you and your palms are facing forward.
- Keeping your chest up and maintaining a slight arch in your lower back, pull the handles down as if you were doing a regular pulldown. The range of motion will be more of an arc. During the movement, rotate your hands so that in the bottom position your palms face each other rather than forward. Return slowly to the starting position and repeat.
